newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia cocoa easier in dull post-harvest trade.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia cocoa easier in dull post-harvest trade.

text.p: Indonesian cocoa prices were easier on Wednesday from a week ago in dull trading in the aftermath of the mid-crop harvest, traders said.
They said cocoa was mostly quoted at 2,640-2,680 rupiah/kg in Ujung Pandang, capital of the key growing region of South Sulawesi, compared with 2,600-2,630 rupiah a week ago.
But they said some buyers seeking to fulfil contracts amid the thin supply were offering up to 2,700 rupiah/kg.
"There's not much beans to buy at the moment," one trader said. "But some farmers have been coming to me with pods that are not fully ripe because they need money for Eid al-Fitr."
"The pods are still green and will yield very little cocoa butter. So I have been turning them away," the trader said. "The unripe beans are sticky and can clog up the machines."
Another trader said business was expected to remain dull until the main crop harvest in March, but added that some buyers have been trying to fulfill export contracts.

"They are offering on the high side because supply is very thin at the moment," he said. "Several other players have temporarily gone out of the market because of poor prices. I guess they will return when prices improve."
